sections.normalized_html: Given that the point [MATH: A] has coordinates [MATH: (\sqrt 3, 1),] calculate the angle [MATH: \theta.]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/9188a594267e833afe9c922d5b37b07a]

Given that the point [MATH: A] has coordinates [MATH: (\sqrt 3, 1),] calculate the angle [MATH: \theta.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we can form a triangle by creating a vertical line from [MATH: A] to the [MATH: x]-axis.

Using the tangent ratio, we have

[MATH: \tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt 3} = \dfrac{\sqrt 3}{3}.]

Finally, using the inverse tangent, we get

[MATH: \theta = \arctan{\left( \dfrac{\sqrt 3}{3} \right)} = 30^\circ.]
